newsitem.title: USA: Boeing to add about 10,000 jobs this year.
newsitem.headline: Boeing to add about 10,000 jobs this year.

text.p: Boeing Co plans to add about 10,000 jobs to its workforce in 1997 in a sharp slowdown from the hiring spree that saw the company add 21,000 positions in 1996, a company spokesman said Tuesday.
The world's biggest aircraft manufacturer currently employs about 153,000 people, including nearly 6,000 hired so far this year, said Boeing spokesman Peter Conte.
The total also includes about 21,000 employees who joined the company as part of the $3 billion acquisition of Rockwell International Corp's defense and aerospace business.
At the end of 1995, after several waves of layoffs, Boeing employed about 105,000 people, down from a 1989 peak of nearly 166,000.
In early 1996 the company began hiring again, ultimately rehiring most of the people laid off in 1995 and launching an aggressive national recruitment campaign targeted mostly at engineers.
Conte said the recruitment campaign had ended, although the company is continuing to recruit for selective jobs and accept resumes over the Internet.
The projected job totals do not include the planned acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp and its 64,000 employees, which would push Boeing's total headcount to about 220,000.
